Hey bro,

Can I ask what do you mean when you are saying "watching PA" at the zone of interest ( let's make it short - ZOI )? is PA an engulf of opposite direction from where price coming from?

Something like when price getting close/touch/inside the ZOI, you'll want to wait for engulf down (your 4 ZOIs)?

What would it need to engulf that counts as a real engulf (Not FO)? breaking/engulfing last flag? There are flags in all LTFs (M1, M5, M15), which one that you would weight more? Very often I saw that an engulf of M1 flag failed to flip price, and engulf of M15 flag has put price too far and entering will be in the mid way, which is no good (IF said entry should be at extreme).

Also, what happen when price break the first of your ZOI? will you take a trade on the retrace to the DP, and TP at your second ZOI (from bottom up)?

Sorry to ask a lot of questions at once, because I think it's all tightly related...

سلام برادر،

می‌تونم بپرسم منظورت از «تماشای PA» در ناحیهٔ مورد نظر (بذار اسمش رو کوتاه بنویسم - ZOI) چیه؟ PA یعنی یه اینگالف در جهت مخالف جایی که قیمت از اونجا اومده؟

مثلاً وقتی قیمت نزدیک می‌شه/لمس می‌کنه/داخل ZOI می‌شه، می‌خوای منتظر اینگالف نزولی بمونی (4 تا ZOI خودت)؟

چه چیزی باید اینگالف بشه تا به‌حساب اینگالف واقعی بیاد (نه FO)؟ شکستن/اینگالف آخرین فلگ؟ تو همهٔ LTF‌ها (M1, M5, M15) فلگ هست، کدوم رو مهم‌تر می‌دونی؟ خیلی وقتا دیدم اینگالف فلگ M1 نتونست قیمت رو برگردونه، و اینگالف فلگ M15 قیمت رو خیلی دور برد و ورود میانهٔ راه می‌شه که خوب نیست (IF گفت ورود باید تو نقطهٔ اکسترم باشه).

همچنین، وقتی قیمت اولین ZOI تو رو می‌شکنه چی می‌شه؟ روی برگشت به DP معامله می‌گیری و TP رو روی ZOI دوم می‌ذاری (از پایین به بالا)؟

ببخشید که یک‌جا این‌همه سؤال پرسیدم، چون فکر می‌کنم همه‌ش به‌هم گره خورده‌اند…

Form your analysis around interesting and obvious levels, a single chart mark up could involve the following 7 step process: Step 1: Draw a horizontal line along support or resistance. Step 2: Label the engulfs (ENG) of this line when they occur. Step 3: Label the decision points (DP) of those ENG. Step 4: Label the FTRs that form AT or AFTER the DP has formed. Step 5: Observe when price is capped by a DP or FTR...this will give you an idea who is in control, buyers or sellers, whilst keeping you out of bad trades. Step 6: Observe when price engulfs a DP or FTR you have labelled. Step 7: Label the NEW DP. Rinse and repeat.

Now imagine the power when you combine this with multi-timeframe analysis and when you wait for the price action to confirm your bias.

تحلیل خود را حول سطوح جالب و آشکار شکل بده، علامت‌گذاری یک چارت می‌تواند فرایند 7 مرحله‌ای زیر را در بر بگیرد: مرحلهٔ 1: یک خط افقی در امتداد حمایت یا مقاومت بکش. مرحلهٔ 2: اینگالف‌های (ENG) این خط را وقتی رخ می‌دهند برچسب بزن. مرحلهٔ 3: نقاط تصمیم (DP) آن ENG‌ها را برچسب بزن. مرحلهٔ 4: FTR‌هایی که دقیقاً هنگام یا بعد از شکل‌گیری DP شکل می‌گیرند را برچسب بزن. مرحلهٔ 5: لحظه‌ای که قیمت توسط یک DP یا FTR مهار می‌شود را زیر نظر بگیر… این به تو ایده می‌دهد چه کسی کنترل را در دست دارد، خریداران یا فروشندگان، و در عین حال تو را از معاملات بد دور نگه می‌دارد. مرحلهٔ 6: لحظه‌ای که قیمت یک DP یا FTR را که برچسب زده‌ای اینگالف می‌کند را زیر نظر بگیر. مرحلهٔ 7: DP جدید را برچسب بزن. این کار را تکرار کن.

حالا قدرتش را تصور کن وقتی این را با تحلیل چندتایم‌فریمی ترکیب کنی و وقتی منتظر می‌مانی رفتار قیمت جهت‌گیری تو را تأیید کند.

nice article.. qoute from ALPHA OMEGA, is it true?

AlphaOmega said: "Some people here are just wrong in their understanding and theories. The whole assumption that only the buyers and sellers (traders) move the price is just wrong! The fx market in the way it exist today is not pure auction. It's a little bit more complicated. Think of the market as two sides. 1. The SELL side - these are the Liquidity providers and the market makers. 2. The BUY side - these are the liquidity consumers. (all traders, large and small, hedge funds, and all other market participants who trade in order to exchange currency for business/corporate transactions). Over 98% of the fx liquidity is provided by 15-20 banks, and about about 80% that liquidity comes from just the biggest 5-8 banks. The SELL side not only controls the market - they ARE the market, they own it! This is THEIR game. Not the game of the traders(regardless of size). If for some reason the market makers want to move the price 1000 pips in 5 min. - they can do that! The traders CANNOT! When you see the price suddenly jumping like crazy and creating this long big single bars on your chart(usually just after news release), what do you think happened there? You think this a result from huge volumes ( traders buying/selling)?? NO it is NOT!. There is very little volume done during these moment. What actually happens, is market makers pulling/removing their limit orders. (They reduce their risk by providing less liquidity on the risk side of the market). Of course the buy side( the traders) have some influence, but nothing significant. When the news hits the wires, the liquidity providers will be the first to react. That's their job. Then, when there is no news and no risk events, this is the other side of the game called price manipulation and stop hunting - take the lows, take the highs, creating fake breakouts and squeezing traders on both sides. Why market makers doing all this? Because volume = profits for them. If price doesn't move, nobody trades. No volume from the buy side = no profits for the market makers. So they will do anything they can to provoke the traders to trade. They will move the price all day long searching for the buy side. Less than half of the price movement is actual buying/selling from traders".
